newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND TO TENDER FOR HANDLOWY SALE ADVISER IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: POLAND TO TENDER FOR HANDLOWY SALE ADVISER IN 1996.

text.p: Poland will open a tender for an advisor in the sale of the country's biggest commercial Bank Handlowy SA this year and start privatising it in 1997, deputy finance minister Ryszard Pazura said on Wednesday.
Pazura told Reuters the ministry would offer 30 percent of the bank's shares to large institutional foreign and domestic investors, but gave no further details.
"The finance ministry will open a tender for the privatisation adviser in the sale of Bank Handlowy still this year," Pazura said.
"We would like to offer 30 percent of the bank's shares to large institutional investors of renown in Poland and abroad," Pazura said.
Earlier this month the government has signalled it would likely decide on the method of Handlowy privatisation in November and the sell-off could take place by mid-1997.

Handlowy's net profit in the first half of this year rose 41.7 percent to 390.3 million zlotys from the same period of 1995. Its balance sheet total rose to 10.46 billion zlotys from 9.93 at the end of 1995 and 7.15 billion in mid-1995.
